newsitem.title: CHINA: China platinum, diamond sales seen up in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China platinum, diamond sales seen up in 1997.

text.p: Sales of platinum and diamond jewellery in China are expected to reach new highs in 1997 as Chinese incomes rise, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
"The Chinese market has enormous potential considering its large population and growing living standard," the newspaper quoted Luan Bingao, vice-chairman of the China Gemology Association, as saying.
Sales of platinum and diamond jewellery were seen hitting new highs in 1997, Luan said, adding that more people were expected to buy diamonds as engagement rings.
"While many Chinese mistakingly regarded platinum as silver or stainless steel only a few years ago, an increasing number have realised the metal's true value," the newspaper said.
China's consumer market for diamond jewellery was now the largest in Asia after Japan, the newspaper quoted South African diamond giant De Beers Consolidated Mines Ltd as saying.

In China's capital Beijing, platinum and diamond jewellery priced at 3,000-4,000 yuan ($360-$480) was the best seller while that priced from 5,000-6,000 yuan was also popular, the newspaper quoted Luan as saying.

The average annual income of residents in China's 35 major cities was 5,059 yuan in 1995 while the average income of rural residents, who account for about 75 percent of China's 1.2 billion people, was 1,578, official figures show.
China has no known platinum deposits and most of the metal on the domestic market was imported from Hong Kong, the newspaper said.
Although China produced some 150,000 carats of diamonds a year for domestic consumption, its jewellery industry still relied on imports from Israel, Belgium and Hong Kong, it said.
China had 80 diamond-cutting factories, mainly in the southern province of Guangdong, eastern Shandong province and Shanghai, it said but gave no further details.
